stories.headline: Best scenes, moments from Valkyries' first championship parade
stories.summary: Feel and relive the best moments from the Valkyries' first championship parade in franchise history.
stories.body:
All it took was two years to bring the city out.

Last weekend, the Golden State Valkyries ended the Atlanta Dream's hopes of winning their first title when they knocked off the Angel Reese-led squad 68-63 in the first Game 7 in WNBA history.

And to celebrate, just like any other championship-winning franchise, they're taking their trophy through downtown to celebrate Wednesday.

The parade, which will take place in San Francisco, will begin at noon PT and go until 2 p.m. Its route will start at the Ferry Building near Mission Street and will end at King and 2nd Street, according to the franchise.

"Our fans have been with us since day one. They sold out every game, traveled with us and made Ballhalla one of the best environments in sports. This parade is our chance to celebrate this championship with all of them," Valkyries president Jess Smith said in a statement.

The Valkyries debuted as a franchise in 2024 and now, two years later, they became the third team across the NBA, BAA and WNBA to win a title within their first two seasons as a franchise, according to Elias Sports Bureau. They also became the first WNBA team to win a title despite not having any All-WNBA players on their roster.

Now, they have the ultimate achievement to celebrate. Here are the best sights and sounds from the Valkyries' championship parade.

stories.headline: Liverpool bemoan 'cheap, messy goals' in loss at Fenerbahce
stories.summary: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola bemoaned his side's poor defending of set pieces leading to "cheap, messy" goals which cost them a 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce.
stories.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola bemoaned his side's poor defending of set pieces leading to "cheap, messy" goals which cost them a 3-2 defeat and the loss of their 100% Champions League record against Fenerbahce on Wednesday.

On a chaotic night in Istanbul, the visitors twice conceded the lead given to them by Trey Nyoni -- scoring his first goal for the club -- and Alexander Isak, with goals from Englishmen Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown before Vedat Muriqi scored a 79th-minute winner.

It was the first time they had conceded three in three successive European games, extending their woeful record in Türkiye to just one win, one draw and seven defeats and they have yet to keep a clean sheet in the country, which also extends to Champions League and Super Cup finals.

"Cheap goals. Messy goals," Iraola said in his postgame news conference.

"The free kick is quite far out, through the wall. The last goal was a long throw, the second one Cody [Gakpo] touched the ball just in front of Ali [goalkeeper Alisson Becker].

"In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate, it was difficult for me to give instructions and the communication was difficult between Cody and Ali."

After five successive wins in all competitions they have now lost back-to-back games, but this defeat was far more damaging to morale than Sunday's reverse to Arsenal.

Set-pieces were an Achilles heel last season, but Liverpool had seemingly rectified that this term before collapsing against a team who had been hammered 6-0 by Aston Villa last month.

"We conceded from a free kick, a corner, a long throw and that has hurt us," Iraola added. "We have gone in front twice, we conceded in situations we should have definitely done better [with].

"We have been dealing well with these situations up to today. It has cost us. We have to do better."

Iraola defended his team selection after making five changes from Sunday, including starting with Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo on the bench before introducing them in the second half.

"We have done this not just today, we have done it all season. All the games midweek we have been changing four or five as it's impossible to retain the starting XI," Iraola added.

"I trust the squad to sustain the level and I don't think it is the main reason why we lost. We have to look more at how we conceded the goals as the reason we didn't win."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Juventus eye moves for Šeško, Balogun
stories.summary: Juventus are keeping tabs on possible moves for forwards Benjamin Šeško and Folarin Balogun. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Šeško and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun, while Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena has caught the eye of Arsenal. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Šeško and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun, with plans to land a striker in January, Calciomercato reports. The Serie A club are keen to acquire a physical front man in the next transfer window, when they are expected to have around €100 million available to reinforce their squad. Šeško, 23, hasn't featured for United since Sept. 16 in the EFL Cup against Brighton & Hove Albion due to injury, while a move for 25-year-old Balogun could be possible after Monaco accepted an initial €40m offer from Everton in the summer before the deal fell through.

- Arsenal are keeping tabs on Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena, TEAMtalk reports. An offer worth €80 million is expected to be required to secure the 25-year-old's transfer, as the Gunners explore the market for a top option to play on the left flank. The Premier League side could face competition from Bayern Munich for Baena, who has scored five goals and provided three assists in 11 LaLiga matches this season. Arsenal could raise funds for this with the exit of midfielder Martín Zubimendi, amid interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old has struggled to start regularly since the arrival of Bruno Guimarães and the Gunners would want a fee around the €60m that they parted with to land him from Real Sociedad in July 2025.

- Manchester United are considering a move for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney as they prioritize adding depth at the No. 9 position, according to Football Insider. The Red Devils are monitoring the 30-year-old, who has scored 12 goals in nine Saudi Pro League matches this season, with several other options also on their shortlist. Toney has been in Saudi Arabia since joining Al Ahli from Brentford in the summer of 2024.

- Barcelona are interested in Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall, according to Football Insider. Bergvall, 20, chose Spurs over Barcelona in 2024, but the Blaugrana are still monitoring him, though Spurs are in control of his future as his contract is not set to expire until the summer of 2031. The Sweden international has made four Premier League appearances this season and has also emerged on the radar of Napoli.

- Al-Hilal have ended their pursuit of Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes, TalkSPORT reports. The Saudi Pro League club were strongly linked with a move for the 32-year-old over the summer, but they aren't expected to make a new approach for him in January, with no plans to free up any of their overseas player slots. Fernandes, yet to reach an agreement over a new contract at Old Trafford, has eight months remaining on his deal.

Other rumors

- Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain have made recent inquiries for Chelsea winger Estêvão. (TEAMtalk)

- Benfica are interested in Monza striker Gustavo Varela, 21, but there is strong competition emerging from Arsenal, Napoli and Barcelona. (A Bola)

- AC Milan have joined the race for Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Minnesota United forward Kelvin Yeboah is on the radar of Everton. (Football Insider)

- USMNT defender George Campbell is in talks with West Brom regarding a contract extension. (Mike McGrath)

- Sunderland midfielder Noah Sadiki is attracting interest from Liverpool, Newcastle, Napoli, and Juventus. (Ekrem Konur)

- Brighton remain keen on FC Köln winger Said El Mala. (Florian Plettenberg)

- Liverpool will look to offload attacking midfielder Harvey Elliott if Valencia terminate his current loan in January. (Football Insider)

- Monza and Pisa are exploring loan moves for AC Milan forward Francesco Camarda. (Nicolò Schira)

stories.headline: ESPN's AFL Misery Index: Which club would you have least wanted to support since 2000?
stories.summary: Which AFL club has had the most success since the turn of the century? Which teams' fans have had a miserable existence since 2000? We've ranked each club on our Misery Index.
stories.body:
Which AFL club would you have wanted to support most since the turn of the century? Of course, the answer to that question has to be your own team, but if we did get a second choice, who would you pick? In other words, which club has provided its fanbase with the most happiness? On the flip side, which team has provided the most disappointment?

Welcome to ESPN's AFL Misery Index.

This is a countdown of the teams that have given its fans with the least amount of joy since 2000. I'm not just looking at premierships and win percentages, but also finals records, droughts, off-field issues, as well as the ability to draft well and attract free agents.

Let's get into it, beginning with the team you would have most wanted to support!

18. Geelong
Record: 422-6-217 (65.9%)

Premierships: 4

Finals series/finals: 21/53

Bottom four finishes: 0

The Cats may not have won as many flags as the Lions in this period but what this club has going for it is sustained relevance and competitiveness since basically the turn of the century. Geelong just doesn't know how to be bad and if you're a fan born in 2000 you would have already witnessed your team win four premierships, play in seven Grand Finals, and feature in a staggering 15 preliminary finals. The Cats have also had more stability than anyone else, with just two coaches in the last 26 years. And to cap off the perfect supporter experience, Geelong is now just about the destination club for free agents and homesick Victorians.

17. Brisbane

Record: 331-6-297 (52.7%)

Premierships: 6

Finals series/finals: 14/41

Bottom four finishes: 8

Some will argue vehemently that it's insane to not have the Lions sitting top of this list given the club has won six premierships (and completed two separate three-peats) since 2000. Granted, that's more success than anyone else, and it's not particularly close. But between these two modern day dynasties, Brisbane was a complete rabble. In fact, the club featured in finals just once from 2005 to 2018 -- that's half of the period we're taking into consideration here! You'd love to have supported this mob, no doubt, but the Cats simply have to pip them for top spot based on their significantly higher floor.

16. Hawthorn
Record: 351-6-274 (56.1%)

Premierships: 4

Finals series/finals: 15/38

Bottom four finishes: 4

Of all the dynasties we've witnessed since the turn of the century, was Hawthorn's the best? There's a real argument to be made the dominance of this club, under Alastair Clarkson, tops anything else we've seen in recent times. The Hawks were the envy of the competition between 2008 and 2015, winning four flags with one of the greatest teams ever assembled. You'd be pretty thrilled going to the footy each week and watching both Lance Franklin and Cyril Rioli running around in your forward line! With Zach Merrett and Ben King being added to the mix this current offseason, Hawthorn is once again a premiership favourite.

15. Sydney
Record: 380-6-254 (59.8%)

Premierships: 2

Finals series/finals: 21/47

Bottom four finishes: 2

When you consider the Swans have played in seven of the last 21 Grand Finals and own the second-best win percentage since 2000, there's a strong argument they should rank higher on this list. But, of course, five of those Grand Finals ended in heartbreaking defeat. In the last two Grand Final losses, they've been belted off the park. That really stings! As does the recent Pullman Hotel saga involving a number of the club's most high-profile players. Still, there would be many footy fans selling their souls to the devil to have what the Swans have had this millennium.

14. Collingwood
Record: 361-8-267 (57.4%)

Premierships: 2

Finals series/finals: 17/43

Bottom four finishes: 4

The Magpies have provided their passionate fanbases with real bang for their supporter buck over the last 26 years. Of course, there's been six Grand Finals and two memorable triumphs, but also 17 finals series and 12 preliminary final appearances. Basically, just about one in every two years Collingwood is still alive at preliminary final weekend! The club has also avoided bottoming out and made a habit of immediately catapulting itself back up the ladder whenever they've suffered a down season. Say what you want about the Magpies army, but they've certainly experienced happiness since 2000.

13. Richmond
Record: 272-9-331 (45.2%)

Premierships: 3

Finals series/finals: 9/19

Bottom four finishes: 9

What an incredible four-year period it was for the Tigers between 2017 and 2020 where it played in three Grand Finals and won all three. Talk about capitalizing on your premiership window! From a fan perspective, the best part of the era might have been getting to watch three-time Norm Smith Medal winner and club legend Dustin Martin play each of his 302 games. However, outside of that dominant four-year block, Richmond managed to win just one final (in 2001) and finished in the bottom four on nine occasions, three times collecting the wooden spoon. Things also don't appear to be improving any time soon.

12. West Coast
Record: 291-4-327 (47.1%)

Premierships: 2

Finals series/finals: 14/29

Bottom four finishes: 9

Since 2000, the Eagles have played in four Grand Finals, winning two and losing two. Both flags were incredibly memorable. In 2006, West Coast got its revenge against Sydney, winning the thrilling decider by a solitary point. In 2018, they stormed over the top of Collingwood, a game that will forever be remembered for Dom Sheed's late brilliance in the pocket. Had it not been for an absolutely dire last five years -- arguably the worst 100-game stretch in the AFL era -- this club would probably have been in the top four. Still, Eagles fans continue to show up and support the club through its dark times.

11. Western Bulldogs
Record: 307-5-308 (49.9%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 13/27

Bottom four finishes: 5

The Bulldogs are usually there or there abouts. A memorable breakthrough flag in 2016 provided so much joy to the loyal fanbase that had been starved of success for so long. They then returned to the Grand Final in 2021, losing to the Demons in the west. Before the Luke Beveridge era, the Bulldogs also enjoyed a strong patch under Rodney Eade, reaching three consecutive preliminary finals between 2008 and 2010. This club continues to employ Marcus Bontempelli, one of the greatest players of the generation, and just landed superstar midfielder Zak Butters. There's plenty to be chuffed about if you support the Dogs.

10. Port Adelaide
Record: 333-3-288 (53.6%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 13/31

Bottom four finishes: 4

This club has played in two Grand Finals since the turn of the century. The first, in 2004, resulted in a premiership and denied Brisbane a fourth successive flag. The second, in 2007, resulted in the greatest loss in Grand Final history, a 119-point defeat at the hands of Geelong. Port Adelaide has not been back to the big dance since that day but under Ken Hinkley they were a picture of consistency for a decade, reaching four preliminary finals since 2014. Did you know that only Geelong, Sydney, Collingwood, and Hawthorn have won more games than the Power since 2000?

9. Adelaide
Record: 330-2-289 (53.3%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 14/29

Bottom four finishes: 4

The Crows have been average to decent for much of the last 26 years, which has to rank them somewhere in the middle. How does ninth sound?! This club has the best winning percentage since 2000 of teams that haven't won a premiership in the period, and sixth-best overall. They have also claimed three minor premierships in that time and outside of the shortened 2020 season haven't ever really had a bad year. But despite all of that, Adelaide has only featured in one Grand Final (where it started as a significant favourite and lost). That 2017 heartbreak against Richmond was followed by an infamous pre-season camp and seven-year September drought.

8. Melbourne
Record: 266-4-343 (43.7%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 10/20

Bottom four finishes: 8

The 2021 premiership is doing plenty of heavy lifting for the Demons here. In fact, without that flag there's a real argument Melbourne should be on the bottom of this list. From 2005 to 2017 this club experienced the lowest of lows, routinely belted off the park and never coming close to playing finals. Who can ever forget that humiliating 186-point loss to the Cats in 2011 -- the second-greatest defeat in league history? But all (well, most) was forgotten with that breakthrough flag at Optus Stadium, though that in itself was a sore point for many of the Demons faithful who missed out on witnessing it in the flesh! The fact this club still hasn't won a final since that day is wildly disappointing.

7. Fremantle
Record: 304-3-308 (49.7%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 10/22

Bottom four finishes: 5

After this year's extraordinary Grand Final capitulation against Brisbane, maybe it wouldn't be outrageous for the Dockers to be at the bottom of this list. After all, has anything more demoralizing ever happened to a footy team on the field? I'm not so sure. It's now two Grand Finals Fremantle has played in and on both days they could probably consider themselves the better team. Yet the club still awaits its inaugural premiership. The fact the Dockers' list is in such a great spot right now, and is set up for the next half decade (at least) probably saves them from dropping a few more rungs here.

6. St Kilda
Record: 282-8-323 (46.7%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 9/20

Bottom four finishes: 6

Saints fans will argue they must be lower on this list, but remember, we're only talking from 2000 onwards. Since the turn of the century, this club has featured in three Grand Finals. Sure, one of them was a replay, and they were unable to win any of them, but simply being in those positions is far more than can be said for any of those ranking below them. What's incredibly tough to swallow for St Kilda supporters is seeing the club fall agonisingly short when they were competitive, a period which has been sandwiched by prolonged middling stretches. In other words, irrelevance.

5. GWS
Record: 164-4-180 (47.7%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 8/19

Bottom four finishes: 4

Remember when the media was convinced the Giants were going to win the next 10 premierships? Well, that aged like milk. GWS currently sits on zero flags, but the club did feature in the 2019 Grand Final, a day they were humiliated by Richmond. And then of course there was the home semifinal loss to eventual premier Brisbane in 2024, a game in which they led by 44 points. Oh, and the heartbreaking 2016 home preliminary final loss to the Bulldogs, another eventual premier. This club has had no shortage of talent but nothing to show for it. Its two best players, Jeremy Cameron and Toby Greene, have also both ultimately wanted to leave.

4. Essendon
Record: 276-7-328 (45.7%)

Premierships: 1

Finals series/finals: 11/18

Bottom four finishes: 8

Essendon's 2000 premiership might well have saved the club from last spot on this list, because since then they have basically lurched from one disaster to the next. There was heartbreak the following year with a Grand Final defeat to Brisbane, before three consecutive semifinal losses. The Bombers have now not won a final in 22 years, something that's become a meme in footy circles. Essendon also endured the biggest off-field saga this century with its involvement in the infamous supplements saga that led to coach sackings and player suspensions, setting the club back years. To cap it off, captain Zach Merrett begged to be traded, wasn't, and then was. Grim.

3. North Melbourne
Record: 256-5-349 (42.4%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 9/17

Bottom four finishes: 10

No team has finished in the bottom four more times since 2000 than North Melbourne. Even the 'good' periods were hardly worth celebrating, back-to-back preliminary final losses in 2014 and 2015 were followed by an elimination final loss in 2016 and then a dreadful, competition-worst 10-year finals drought. The Kangaroos have had nine coaches (Jaymie Graham will be the 10th) in the last 26 years and in many ways have forgotten what it feels like to win. The fact Nick Blakey is seen as the club's saviour proves attracting free agents and marquee signings has been slim pickings for this mob.

2. Carlton
Record: 242-6-362 (40.2%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 9/17

Bottom four finishes: 9

From the salary cap breach and draft pick punishment to a merry-go-round of coaches, there's been setback after setback for the Blues in the 21st century. This club has claimed a league-high five wooden spoons since 2000 (they had zero prior to 2000) and forced its fans to witness its most barren and disappointing stretch in history. The best moment in 26 years was a stirring semifinal win over Melbourne in 2023, which tells you all you need to know about how much this club has been starved of success in the modern era.

1. Gold Coast
Record: 114-2-237 (32.6%)

Premierships: 0

Finals series/finals: 1/2

Bottom four finishes: 9

Question: what's this club's greatest moment in history? Answer: a one-point win over Fremantle in an elimination final in 2025. Literally every other team has enjoyed a significantly higher peak this century, which has to place the Suns dead last on our ranking. That memorable final was one of just two finals Gold Coast has ever played and the only finals series it has qualified for (everyone else has at least eight in this time!). Season 2025 remains the only campaign in which the Suns won more games than they lost. Gold Coast also has easily the worst winning percentage of any club. Yeah, supporting this team has brought basically zero happiness.

stories.headline: Athletics hire Brewers' Cam Castro as new general manager
stories.summary: The Athletics have hired the Brewers' Cam Castro to be their new GM. Castro served as Milwaukee's senior vice president of player development and performance.
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Athletics president of baseball operations Taylor Smith made his first major decision since taking over two weeks ago, going to World Series champion Milwaukee to hire Cam Castro on Wednesday as general manager.

Castro, 36, was the Brewers' senior vice president of player development and performance. He was with the club for eight years, serving as the liaison between the front office and the coaching staff regarding player development.

"The A's are a historic franchise with an incredible legacy," Castro said in a statement. "I look forward to being a part of the next chapter of A's baseball and developing a team, culture and organization that our fans will be proud of."

The A's, who went 64-98 this season, are rebuilding their front office in anticipation of the organization's planned moved to Las Vegas in 2028. They are scheduled to play their third and final season next year at a Triple-A ballpark in West Sacramento, California.

Hiring Smith, who previously was with the Red Sox and Rays, began that makeover.

"Cam will be an awesome addition to the front office and a great partner to me in running this organization," Smith said in a statement. "He has experiences and skillsets that will complement me and the very talented people that we already have in the organization. He's one of the best development minds in the game with a proven track record of building the systems and processes that develop a winner."

stories.headline: Voters reject tax proposal tied to plans for Stars' new arena
stories.summary: Texas voters rejected a proposal to authorize taxes to help pay off $700 million in bonds for a proposed $3 billion development that includes an arena for the Stars.
stories.body:
PLANO, Texas -- Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL's Stars.

Unofficial results from Tuesday's vote in the city of Plano showed 54.6% of the more than 102,000 votes cast were against the single ballot proposal to authorize taxes on tickets, parking, car rentals, hotel rooms and the professional teams that would use the arena. Those taxes were to help the city pay off up to $700 million in bonds it has committed to the proposed $3 billion mixed-use development that would include the new arena.

The vote was about the proposed taxes, and not whether the $1 billion arena could be built as part of a large-scale redevelopment project of The Shops at Willow Bend, where the last enclosed mall built in Texas is being demolished. It could include sports, entertainment, retail, dining and public gathering spaces.

"The proposed redevelopment at The Shops at Willow Bend remains an important opportunity for our community," Plano Mayor John Muns said in a statement. "We are committed to thoughtful reinvestment and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars as we consider what comes next."

The hockey-specific arena would be owned by the city, with the Stars intending to lease it for 30 years.

Stars officials hope to move in 2031 about 20 miles north of the downtown American Airlines Center, which they have shared with the NBA's Dallas Mavericks since it opened in 2001. The leases at the AAC for both teams expire in 2031, and the Mavericks have plans for a similar project of their own away from downtown, about 10 miles north on the former site of a Dallas mall.

stories.headline: Charles Leclerc to miss Brazilian Grand Prix media duty due to birth of baby
stories.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc will miss media duties ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix following the birth of his first child.
stories.body:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc will miss media duties ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix following the birth of his first child.

The Monagesque driver announced on Instagram that his wife Alexandra gave birth to their daughter Bianca on Tuesday.

Leclerc had been scheduled to answer questions from the press on Thursday but has been allowed extra time at home with his family in Monaco.

The 29-year-old's absence means he will not address criticism from team-mate Lewis Hamilton following their tussle in the Mexico Grand Prix last weekend.

Hamilton accused Leclerc of working against him after he tried to overtake the British driver during the first lap when the pair were in front, opening the door for Max Verstappen to win the race.

"We have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure," Hamilton said.

- Kimi Antonelli to shun number one on car for 2027 season as new F1 champion wants to 'stay humble'

- Lewis Hamilton: Watching successor Kimi Antonelli win title 'highlight of my year'

- George Russell admits his F1 season had 'more bad days than good' following Kimi Antonelli championship triumph

"We don't have rules of engagement and, whether or not that will change anything from Charles' side, I don't know. Something needs to change for sure.

"I think it's a mentality thing. It's like, 'Do or die. Either I win or none of us do,' and it shouldn't be that."

The spat was met with frustration by Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur, who told Sky Sports: "I think it's just a matter of respect. Honestly, it's difficult to digest for me to give up a win like this."

stories.headline: Robert Lewandowski's jersey outselling Lionel Messi's since Chicago arrival
stories.summary: Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in MLS since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Miami kit.
stories.body:
Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in Major League Soccer since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Inter Miami kit.

MLS' 10 best-selling jerseys of 2026 was revealed by the league on Tuesday, with Messi still No. 1 overall but with former Barcelona and Bayern Munich star Lewandowski making a big impact.

- MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up

- Messi brings Miami back to stun Revs, clinch Champions Cup spot

- Nashville ties Miami's single-season points record with 1 game to go

Lewandowski officially signed with Chicago on June 29, and made his MLS debut on July 22 against Inter Miami.

The Poland international has recorded seven goals and added five assists in 18 games, propelling the Fire to fourth place on the Eastern Conference table and a place in the playoffs.

Miami captain Messi, however, leads sales through all of 2026, earning first place for the fourth consecutive season. Messi first topped the list in 2023, just months after signing with Inter Miami in July of that year.

This year, just behind Messi, LAFC's Son Heung-Min stands in second place and Vancouver Whitecaps forward Thomas Müller in third.

The list was based on sales made on MLS' online store from Jan. 1 through Oct. 30.

New Orlando City player Antoine Griezmann made the list in fifth place after being announced as a new signing in March but officially joining MLS in July upon completing the 2025-26 season with Atlético Madrid.

In sixth place was rising United States star Cavan Sullivan's Philadelphia Union jersey. Sullivan, 17, became the youngest scorer for the U.S. men's national team last month when he found the net against Mexico.

stories.headline: Luana Santos comes to grips with rise in women's bantamweight rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Luana Santos stuck with her strongest fighting skill -- grappling -- in Saturday's UFC fight with fellow top-10 women's bantamweight Yana Santos. Her perseverance paid off. After all nine of her takedown attempts were fended off in the first round, Santos went right back to leaning on her judo background in the two rounds that followed, landing five takedowns and amassing 7½ minutes of control time and winning her fourth fight in a row.

As a result, Luana Santos climbs two spots to No. 5 in the ESPN women's bantamweight rankings, while previously fifth-ranked Yana Santos drops one position to No. 6.

That is the only change in the latest divisional rankings. Women's bantamweight does have change on the horizon, though, as UFC champion Kayla Harrison, unranked because she has not fought in over a year and is ineligible, takes on former two-division champion Amanda Nunes on Nov. 14 at UFC 334. Nunes is coming off a retirement of nearly 3½ years.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

Results are current; rankings as of Nov. 3. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

stories.headline: North Sydney Bears royalty lands in Perth to lead new NRL club
stories.summary: Tony Rea is a man who doesn't mince his words and has been entrusted as the Perth Bears' new chief executive as the club prepares to make its NRL debut.
stories.body:
Former North Sydney Bears captain Tony Rea has landed in Perth as the expansion club's new chief executive following the messy departure of predecessor Anthony De Ceglie.

De Ceglie, a former director of news and current affairs at Seven West Media, stepped down as Perth Bears chief executive last month amidst reports he had lost support of the club's board.

His departure came six months after the club's general manager of football David Sharpe quit after reportedly falling out with several key figures.

The Bears, who will become the NRL's 18th franchise when they make their debut next season, will be hoping Rea brings a sense of calm.

And while De Ceglie had no background in rugby league, Rea can be considered as Bears royalty.

The 60-year-old made 120 appearances for the North Sydney Bears between 1988-94, captaining the club during their run to the 1991 preliminary final.

Rea then moved to England where he became a key figure at the London Broncos, serving roles as a player, coach and chief executive.

He also had a stint as an interim coach of the Brumbies in 2011 following the sacking of Andy Friend just two games into the season.

Rea proved he was a man who didn't mince his words during that stint, unleashing on not only his players but the organisation itself - following a shock 29-20 home loss to the Lions.

"We have just too many people and an organisation that makes too many soft decisions too often, and now they're the bulk and the norm," Rea said at the time.

"It's in the wood now. We have been covering them for a while."

The Perth Bears are yet to secure a superstar recruit ahead of the club's 2027 NRL debut.

But given the November 1 player market has now opened, Rea has the chance to add some much-needed star power to the squad.

"I've sat in almost every seat in a club: player, captain, development officer, head coach, director of rugby and board member," Rea said after landing the Perth Bears role.

"My job as CEO is not to do any one of those jobs but rather to use that experience to lead our professional team together as one, committed to success.

"The Perth Bears have assembled an exceptional and professional team. They have achieved so much in such a short amount of time and I look forward to leading them as CEO into this next chapter."

stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The WNBA Finals were the most watched since 1999, with an average of 1.88 million people viewing the series that Golden State won over Atlanta in a decisive Game 7.

That game averaged 3.3 million viewers, making it the most-watched WNBA postseason game ever. It was up 128% from last season's clinching game between Las Vegas and Phoenix that the Aces won.

All seven games in the series were sold out, including Game 6, which was played at 12:30 p.m. EDT.

The Finals capped the WNBA's most-watched postseason since its inaugural season in 1997, averaging 1.49 million viewers, up 27% from last year.

stories.headline: Colts' Shane Steichen defends Jonathan Taylor usage, says RB will keep role
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor will continue to play his usual role with the Colts despite being at the center of trade talks with multiple teams, Shane Steichen said.
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor will continue to play his usual role despite being at the center of trade talks with multiple teams, coach Shane Steichen said Tuesday.

Steichen was pressed about the organization's approach with Taylor, who played 38 snaps in the Colts' 42-7 loss Sunday to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Steichen said there has been no change to the Colts' plan for Taylor in Week 9 against the Dallas Cowboys.

"There's a lot of stuff out there right now," Steichen said of speculation surrounding Taylor. "He's on our football team and he's excited for this opportunity to go play. He wants to go win this game."

Taylor has attracted trade interest from numerous teams since the Colts (2-6) signaled in recent weeks that they are directing their focus toward the future. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last month and traded highly respected veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week.

Relatedly, receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, though he also played last Sunday and is expected to play against Dallas.

"I'm focused on now," Downs said Wednesday. "We play the Cowboys this week. We have practice today. We're trying to go out there and win. ... I've got to focus on now. That's what's most important."

Steichen acknowledged the Arizona Cardinals' recent decision to hold Marvin Harrison Jr. out of a game after a trade involving the receiver had been agreed to with the Houston Texans. But Steichen said there have been no conversations to that effect between him and the Colts' front office.

"During this time of year, people are going to call," he said. "That's just part of the business. But, again, you've got to be a professional and show up to work."

stories.headline: Aston Villa planning long-term future with Unai Emery in message to rivals
stories.summary: Aston Villa have signalled their intention to build their long-term future around manager Unai Emery.
stories.body:
Aston Villa have signalled their intention to build their long-term future around manager Unai Emery.

Villa announced on Wednesday they had held a meeting to discuss strategy beyond 2029, when Emery's current contract is due to expire.

- Hamilton: Outclassed by Barcelona, but Emery's Aston Villa have plenty for Man United to envy

- Aston Villa left with 'lot of things to learn' after defeat in Barcelona

- Prince William, George watch Villa lose at Camp Nou

There has been no confirmation of a new deal, amid reports an agreement is close, but the club said in a statement that "the sporting leadership of Unai Emery" would be central to their long-term plans.

The Spanish coach has been linked with other clubs after making a significant impact since his appointment at Villa Park in 2022.

The statement read: "Aston Villa held an important working meeting today to plan the club's future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project.

"The meeting brought together Nassef Sawiris, the club's chairman, and Unai Emery alongside president of football operations Roberto Olabe and director of football operations Damian Vidagany.

"The discussions focused on jointly planning the club's long-term strategic direction, with positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery based on the shared ambitions and common goal to reach excellency and keep growing during the next years.

"The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements."

The statement comes a week after Villa had threatened legal proceedings against former England international Jamie Carragher, who told the "Stick to Football" podcast fans should "shut the f--- up" having faced criticism for suggesting Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job.

Carragher has since apologised, saying he used "clumsy and wrong" language, and Villa will not take further action.

Emery oversaw Europa League success last season and has twice led Villa to Champions League qualification.

stories.headline: Every AFL club's 2026 draft plans, prospects linked, and live trade options
stories.summary: ESPN's AFL Draft expert Jasper Chellappah looks at every club's plans, its prospects linked, and potential live trade options.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL Draft is two weeks away, and there's a clearer picture on what each club's draft plans are.

You can expect around 65 selections to be made in what has become a deep draft. The mix from 15 to 30 is incredibly even, and the prospects deserving of an opportunity at AFL level runs well past the 65 picks that we'll see across the nights of November 19 and 20.

Amongst the club intel and prospects being targeted at each pick are potential trades to watch for on draft night. Port Adelaide, Carlton and Brisbane will be beholden to where bids land for their star academy prospects, and the selections they hold could be on the move in live draft night trades. Collingwood, Essendon and Adelaide are amongst the clubs mooted to be interested in trading up the order to secure their targets.

It's worth noting that the arrival of Tasmania has repercussions on this year's draft; clubs are more keen to get in now to secure young talent, but it also means draft capital is worth less in future years. Trading up the draft order will be as hard as it's ever been in the live trade era, meaning we could see a host of potential trades never come to fruition.

Included in the details on the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles are the start of second round compensation picks they will receive at the beginning of night two. These come about after a club-tied prospect -- which will be Port Adelaide's Dougie Cochrane -- is taken with a pick prior to their top five selections.

As we approach November's AFL Draft, these are the draft plans, prospects linked, and live trade options for all 18 clubs.

Adelaide
Draft picks: 15, 32, 35, 43, 56, 92, 110

List needs: Midfield quality, outside speed

Adelaide had a quiet trade period and knocked back a swathe of picks for Nick Murray, meaning Hamish Ogilvie's team holds its natural first-rounder plus two seconds to top up a list hunting a premiership. They're valuable selections, but without any manoeuvring they've left themselves behind two Port Adelaide picks in the second round, amongst a nest of talented SA products. Without making a move on draft night the Power will have first dibs on the local crop.

The Crows had a late NGA application for rebounding defender Jake Eime rejected after being alerted to his Indigenous heritage through the SANFL too late in the piece. That shouldn't dissuade them from using a first-rounder on the local product. Eime has the speed and dare to become an offensive weapon off halfback and improve the quality of ball going inside 50.

They'll likely have one of the top three key defenders in the class available, but it won't be Mitch Harris who is firming as a top 10 selection. Clancy Snell would add to their key defensive depth as a high-upside interceptor out of Gippsland, but it would be a touch early for SA captain Kodah Edwards despite his unique mix of forward impact and contested gruntwork.

The best midfielder available at 15 could be Toby Krasna. The Vic Metro on-baller runs both ways and offers some flair with ball in hand on the outside of contests. The versatility and ready-made body of Lochie Burrows would appeal with a view to eventually playing through the midfield. Potential sliders include athletic third tall Wil Malady and tough WA midfielder Leo Steed; the latter should be right in the frame as a piece to immediately push for senior selection.

Late in the second round the lethal left foot of Wil Antrobus should appeal and Gus Kennedy's toughness as a defender with midfield flashes suits. With Adelaide in need of best 23 contenders through the midfield, local products Archie Van Dyk and Memphis Webb will warrant consideration as mature bodies late in the draft. NGA Anthony Long is a backend draft proposition but has serious tricks in the forward half and is deserving of a main list spot.

Brisbane
Draft picks: 21, 27, 28, 45, 79, 97, 115

List needs: Key defender depth

The Lions have another academy gun on their hands, and Caylen Murray has risen to the precipice of the top 10 this season. Granting Keidean Coleman's trade wish effectively ensured Brisbane would have the collateral to match a bid, but they'll have contingencies in place depending on where it lands.

It could come as early as Queensland rivals Gold Coast at pick 8, which would require 1732 points including a 20% loading on grand finalists. Their first two picks only make up 1254 points right now so the Lions will have moves up and down the board with their three second-rounders depending on where the bid lands.

In Murray they're getting a natural Dayne Zorko replacement with excellent ball skills out of defence. His composure under pressure is a highlight and there are midfield traits to be uncovered at the next level.

If the Lions are able to hold onto a second-rounder Jake Soutar presents as the most ready-made defender in the pool. The 20-year-old took out East Perth's fairest and best this season and plays with fantastic aggression in the air, intercepting and kickstarting transition. Darcy Szerszyn is a similar type in the top 30 mix with good athletic traits but underwent an injury-interrupted year.

Benji Van Rooyen is a long-term ruck prospect to look at towards the end of the draft and at 197cm Tate Hodgson has the defensive aptitude to develop into a reliable key defender.

Carlton
Draft picks: 13, 18, 31, 50, 61, 72, 90, 108

List needs: Classy ball users, long-term ruck

Blues fans have been looking forward to this draft for years. Father-son Cody Walker is a bona fide top pick with elite traits through the midfield and he will land at Princes Park no matter where taken, but it's unlikely to be in the first two selections on draft night.

That's a good result for the Blues with live trades in the works depending on where a bid comes. If it lands at pick 3 they'll require 2178 points and their first two selections will equate to 2019 points after an earlier bid on Cochrane. Carlton can do that with a small deficit on their 2027 first-rounder. If Richmond doesn't bid on Walker and he falls to 4 or 5 there will be clubs keen on those selections, and Carlton can capitalise. A slide back to Essendon's 17 from 13 would allow them to match and move their second-rounder up from 31 to 25.

Getting back into the draft early in the second round will give the Blues access to a group of good ball users including Jackson Phillips and Harvie Cooke. Phillips is the running wingman while Cooke is a high-IQ midfielder with talent to play ahead of the ball. George Dimer and Marlon Neocleous are exciting small forwards to consider and Ethan Herbert is the project ruck around this range.

Later in the piece WA's Benji Van Rooyen could appeal as an apprentice to Marc Pittonet and mature-ager Brady Wright would add immediate competition for spots up forward.

Collingwood
Draft picks: 11, 30, 67, 68, 70, 88, 106

List needs: Midfield speed, key position depth

The Pies own a pick in an exciting spot of the draft. There are a cluster of different prospects deserving of top 10 consideration that will be available, but one that may be gone at that point is Sam Gayfer. The nephew of 1990 premiership defender Mick has steadily risen this year as a pack-splitting key forward and the Pies have been one of his biggest fans. Justin Leppitsch would need to part with at least a future first-rounder to a club like Port Adelaide or Gold Coast to ensure they can get him.

If they stay put, Tyson Bradley appeals as the full back of the future and could play senior football early. He's a strong one-on-one defender and reliable distributor with the character to be a future leader of the club. Clancy Snell put in a good performance for Collingwood's VFL side but is an interceptor that may take more time to develop.

Leo Steed is the pick of the midfielders in this bracket, with the WA on-baller offering a mix of defensive application and contested ball-winning that fits alongside Nick Daicos. High-flying forward Wil Malady will be taken around this mark as well.

In the second round the Pies could look to Harvie Cooke and George Gale as midfield options, and mature-age forward options later in the piece include Brady Wright and Jack Slattery who could add immediate depth behind Jesse Hogan and Dan McStay.

Essendon
Draft picks: 1, 17, 25, 80, 98 (plus second round compensation pick)

List needs: Best available talent

The Bombers are at the bottom of their rebuild and hold the first overall selection a decade after taking Andy McGrath at no. 1. Similarly to 2016 and as opposed to recent drafts, there's no consensus top prospect in the open pool.

Expect a bid on Dougie Cochrane at one which Port Adelaide will quickly match, then the draft really begins. Ethan Drever is the slight favourite at no. 2 after a blistering campaign for club and state. The explosive midfielder stayed injury free and produced gaudy numbers enroute to Vic Country's MVP and GWV Rebels's best and fairest. His elite transition game alongside Dyson Sharp and Sullivan Robey will surely appeal.

Arki Butler is a rare archetype to come through the elite pathways and presents as the forward match-winner of the crop. His name has been firmly in contention for the top spot all season and the need to add talent alongside Nate Caddy in the forward 50 is real. Ruck Harry Van Hattum and classy ball user Heath Mellody deserve consideration here as well, but Drever and Butler have the inside lane two weeks out from the draft.

The Dons will have a look at moving up from 17 with additional picks - that could work for either of Port Adelaide or Carlton live on draft night as they look to maximise their draft hands while still matching bids. The key defensive option in the teens is Tyson Bradley, a no-nonsense negator with leadership plaudits. Toby Krasna is in this range as a talented outside midfielder with flair, while George Dimer is in demand as a speedy small forward with tricks.

In the 20s Essendon should be looking at upside swings. Jack Pickett was the leading key forward prospect coming into the year but a season on the sidelines due to an ACL rupture could make him a bargain on night two. Similarly, Koby LeCras adds size and polish out of WA and Lachie Hicks could prove the midfield steal with his blend of speed and endurance as a former track athlete.

The Dons have some interest in Jake Soutar as a mature-age interceptor to replace Jordan Ridley, but will also need to account for a bid on Blake Justice that likely lands towards the back end of the second round. The NGA graduate has a unique mix of speed and size that could even see him attract a bid early on night two.

Fremantle
Draft picks: 19, 40, 60, 63, 78, 96, 114

List needs: Lockdown defender, high-upside talent

Dockers fans don't need reminding how close they've come to that elusive first premiership, but they've continued to build through the draft and keep their premium picks during contention.

At the end of the first round Jake Eime warrants consideration as a halfback dasher alongside Jordan Clark. He takes the game on with speed and can use the ball well while still defending. Jake Soutar has been closely linked as the mature-age option to add to their best 23, but sits between Freo's first two picks on many boards. They would need to trade up or take him with 19.

With 40 being pushed out on the second night they could look towards local talent in Harvey Spawton-Guy whose competitiveness as a key forward stands out. Tom Brown has been overlooked by some but offers reliability in defence and it would be a brilliant result if hard-running midfielder George Gale was still on the board. The goalkicking prowess of Archie Elliott should also appeal in this range of the draft.

The Dockers will be keen to get Finlay Yeo into the club as buzz continues to grow on the NGA talent. He's gifted below his knees and makes things happen through the midfield and up forward. Cam Maynard has offered mercurial moments as a small forward and finished second in the 20m sprint at the combine, but Lucas Robinson has fallen away this season and will be a rookie consideration for Fremantle.

Geelong
Draft picks: 36, 57, 62, 75, 93, 111

List needs: Defensive depth, high-upside projects

The Cats did their work in the trade period by getting Rowan Marshall and Jordan Ridley into the club. Making those moves is made easier knowing Stephen Wells does his best work late in the draft.

Lachie Hicks presents as the high-upside swing in the second round, similarly to Max Holmes in 2020. Hicks has elite athletic pedigree state records through his juniors in track but also put together an impressive campaign as a midfielder. His ball use is preventing him from being a first round option but there's a lot to work with in a good development program.

Billy Wigmore is an excellent interceptor with a build similar to that of Tom Stewart but his draft range begins earlier than pick 36. Sam Dever has been linked as an athletic utility that looks most at home off halfback at 189cm, while the best local product is Noah Williams who played through frustrating injuries all season. He's a smaller inside midfielder with good defensive instincts that could cut his teeth as a lockdown defender.

Gold Coast
Draft picks: 8, 81, 85, 103

List needs: Key position depth

The Suns have Sam Collins turning 33 next year and lost Ben King to free agency. It leaves them exposed at either end over the next few years and they have real need to address their tall stocks with their first open pool top 10 selection since Bailey Humphrey in 2022.

The best key forward in the draft is Sam Gayfer, a brave aerialist possessing the best vertical jump in combine history. His ability to bring the ball to ground with his pack-crashing attitude should appeal to Damien Hardwick. At the other end Mitch Harris and Clancy Snell offer different styles of key defenders. Harris can lockdown on the best key forwards and intercept in his own right, while Snell is the ultra-aggressive interceptor of the pool. Being a country Victorian will help the Suns when assessing their ability to retain talent.

This is the start of Wil Malady's range in the draft, and there's a chance of a slider like Gus Teixeira or Heath Mellody that could make Gold Coast's choice easy.

Local academy product Archie Hill should find his way onto the list as a running defender that plays with energy and dare.

GWS
Draft picks: 9, 20, 26, 59, 77, 86, 104

List needs: Midfield talent, key position depth

It's all about Ethan Matthews on night one, the best Giants Academy prospect to come through the ranks since Tom Green. Matthews is a classy midfielder that racks it up with clean hands and quick decision making off his preferred left foot, and will deservedly be a top 10 pick.

The Giants are in an awkward spot at pick 9, expecting a bid to land before that selection and potentially coming from crosstown rivals the Swans at pick 6. It makes matching the bid easy but look for them to maximise their draft hand by trading on the clock.

In the middle of the second round they will have a few names on the board. George Dimer should be right up there as a high-character small forward with tricks around goal and a willingness to move interstate. Athletic utility Sam Devers could play anywhere across the ground after a strong finish to an injury-plagued year, while the fascinating call will be on Mason McGroder. The Swans Academy defender has foregone a promising international long jump career to pursue football and although raw boasts elite athletic traits in defence. The Giants could make the Swans sweat with a bid in the 20s for the high-upside athlete.

Hawthorn
Draft picks: 29, 37, 71, 94, 107, 112

List needs: Outside run, halfback depth

The Hawks are beautifully set with depth challenging at just about every position. Bringing in Ben King and Zach Merrett made them the biggest winners of the trade period and they still held onto two valuable selections in a deep draft.

A bid on NGA product Keenan Boi is a chance to arrive before their first pick. The half forward plays through contact with strength and makes good decisions under pressure. He's been likened to Sam Powell-Pepper in his attack on the ball and man in the forward half.

In that second round Harrison Chapman offers a unique blend of strong running at 190cm. He looks most at home on a wing where he can use the ball well in space. Albert MacGowan also has the runs on the board to warrant a second round selection as a high-marking wingman. Wil Antrobus is another who can provide transition run, and comes with the added bonus of an elite left foot out of defence that suits the Hawks's style of play.

Hawthorn will be waiting to see if a bid comes for Cooper Hodge. The son of champion Luke looks most at home in defence but has also had promising outings through the midfield in a potential sign of things to come. If a bid doesn't come in the national draft the Hawks will likely take him with their last pick.

Melbourne
Draft picks: 4, 14, 48, 52

List needs: Key defensive talent, ball-winning midfielders

It's been a perpetual cycle of trading into and up draft boards that has reaped rewards for the Dees, who are building their next generation on the fly. They snagged a top 10 pick from the Suns in the Christian Petracca deal last year and made an early move with Port Adelaide to get even higher up the board.

Now, they're in a fantastic position to snap up one of their top four targets. Names in the mix will include Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody. There's every chance those are the first names off the board in the open pool, and you can expect this to be the final place where a bid on Cody Walker would come.

If those three are gone, there will be a fun mix at the top of their board. Similarly to Luke Jackson in 2019, the Dees could opt to give a ruckman the ultimate apprenticeship under the best to do it in the modern era. Harry Van Hattum is deserving of a pick this high - he blends elite athleticism, skill with ball in hand and physicality at a genuine ruck size. The 205cm enforcer plays with aggression in the mould of Brodie Grundy and, similarly to Grundy, may not have the forward craft to play alongside Gawn early on.

Gus Teixeira is the forward-half midfielder with power and scoreboard impact. He can play through centre bounces but will start his career at half forward where he finds a lot of the ball and doesn't need much space to impact.

The wildcard here is Mitch Harris. The premier defender of the pool is equally adept at locking down and intercepting, playing with an air of calm and composure. His range starts here and the SA product is very much in play for the Demons as a ready-made foil for Jake Lever and Dan Turner with senior football under his belt.

At pick 14 Leo Steed should be right in the mix as an in-and-under midfielder that can run hard both ways on the outside. He plays at a high cadence and has a strong body of work in the WAFL. Toby Krasna and Lochie Burrows are other midfield types that deserve consideration, while the other first-round key defenders in Clancy Snell and Tyson Bradley will be options if they opt against Harris earlier.

Brady Wright or Jack Slattery offer immediate forward depth late in the draft and Marcus Prasad is a small forward with clean hands that the Dees could opt for despite not having rights on through their NGA. Benji Van Rooyen could play alongside his brother as he learns the ropes under Gawn.

North Melbourne
Draft picks: 33, 49, 66, 74, 84, 102

List needs: Key position talent, classy ball users

North put their chips in for Nick Blakey and as a result will be without a top-20 pick for the first time since 2019. It signals a new era for the Shinboners as they mount a charge up the ladder under coach Jaymie Graham.

The Roos enter at pick 33, which will extend out a few spots after bids and compensation picks at the top of night two. Billy Wigmore is the type of defender they've been desperate for - the interceptor can play above his size but also roll off smaller forwards to chop out in the air and assist his key defenders. The third tall could play senior football early to add to North's best 23 depth.

Despite a clear need for key position talent, they've taken Matt Whitlock and Blake Thredgold with premium picks and could instead opt for good ball users around the park with an aim to move the ball with more speed. That puts classy halfback Wil Antrobus in the mix as a weapon to utilise out of defence. Further afield lies the upside of rangy outside midfielder Harrison Chapman who has exciting upside as a transition runner, and this is the range busy small forward Marlon Neocleous is expected to be taken. Albert MacGowan and Sam Devers are other running types that could play senior football next year after strong finishes to the year.

Key forward Aidan McCartney has nominated the Roos as a father-son after being in the Swans Academy and has exciting traits despite being sidelined this year with a hip injury.

Port Adelaide
Draft picks: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46, 65, 101

List needs: Midfield depth, key position talent

Night one is all about Dougie Cochrane, the near-consensus top prospect amongst clubs in 2026. Through the Zak Butters free agency compensation and smart manoeuvring in the trade period the Power are well-prepared to match a bid on the academy star at pick one, and have set themselves up with three first-rounders next year with an eye to Zemes Pilot and Louis Salopek.

Selections 7 and 12 remain on the table, but it will take a significant offer for Port to cop a deficit on their 2027 first-rounder. If they moved 7 down in a trade with St Kilda or Collingwood they would then be dealing with a significant deficit on their 2027 selection, so a trade of pick 12 looks more likely. Adelaide and Essendon can trade up from 15 and 17 respectively without impacting Port's ability to match a bid on Cochrane, which could land the Power a future selection or an extra second-rounder this year.

The second round will have a fun mix of local talent. Halfback dasher Jake Eime would be a priority if he was to slide and SA captain Kodah Edwards is right in the frame. His hands in the contest and scoreboard impact up forward offers unique versatility. Ethan Herbert would be a long-term pick with a view to his upside as a ruckman with fantastic contested numbers, and Gabe Patterson presents as a powerful small forward that can break games open. Ball-winners Archie Van Dyk and Memphis Webb are later propositions that could come on quicker than expected in the right environment.

Outside of SA, Jack Watkins has steadily risen this year and would be a smart choice later in the piece as a goalkicking half forward, while Cody Templeton and Marcus Prasad are other smalls in a similar draft range. WA's George Gale is a big-bodied midfielder with excellent endurance in the Willem Drew mould and ball magnet Jordan Knapp has the midfield chops to make it at the next level despite his slender frame. Both will be right in the mix as Port looks to the next generation of on-ballers. Xavier Ladbrook looms as the best key defensive option outside of the first night but will take time to add the size required to play at AFL level.

Richmond
Draft picks: 2, 5, 44, 99 (plus second round compensation pick)

List needs: Best available talent

The Tigers made a big trade to land a second top five pick and maximise their talent before Tasmania enters the competition. It gives them an enviable hand but they'll need to be smart in how they play it with West Coast and Melbourne picking between their selections.

They've been closely linked to Harry Van Hattum. If they have HVH at the top of the board they'll need to use pick 2 on him, with his aggression making him a natural successor to skipper Toby Nankervis. There's every chance they have another name or two ahead of Van Hattum, however, which means intel on Melbourne will be vital here. There's no guarantee he will be available at 5, but that's the limits of his draft range with Richmond to pounce if still on the board.

All of Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody will be considered at pick 2. Drever is the explosive midfielder that fits comfortably alongside Sam Lalor and Taj Hotton as the midfield of the future. Arki Butler is the much-needed firepower up forward to pair with their project talls, and Mellody provides the class and running power off halfback and through the midfield that has been lacking under Adem Yze.

If Drever is taken by Essendon, Butler will be the live favourite to land at Tigerland. He has been at the pointy end of the draft all season as a mercurial forward in the Toby Greene mould.

Van Hattum is the ideal selection if he gets through to pick 5, but Gus Teixeira has plenty of fans and remains in this section of the crop as a damaging forward-half midfielder with power and scoreboard impact.

The Tigers will add a second round pick to their arsenal through a compensation pick on night two and it's a good spot to add run and dare on the outside. Jackson Phillips has a high floor as a wingman with clean hands and good foot skills, George Gale offers a bigger body and the running power to play peripheral positions and Jake Eime should be a real consideration if he slips through as a speedster out of the backline.

NGA prospect Tanner Armstrong may get through to the category B rookie list.

St Kilda
Draft picks: 10, 16, 41, 51, 69, 87, 105

List needs: Key position depth, inside ball-winner

The Saints have undergone a list transformation over the past few years and now own two quality picks after dealing Rowan Marshall to Geelong. They're in a great position to address areas of need and appear unlikely to trade up from these spots.

At pick 10 local product Tyson Bradley will be right in the frame. He has the body to play senior football at some point next year and is reliable in his defensive instincts and composed ball use. He would immediately compete for a spot alongside Cal Wilkie and Jack Silvagni. At the other end of the ground Sam Gayfer and Wil Malady are very different types of key forward prospects. Gayfer is brave and strong in the air with the biggest leap recorded in combine history. Malady can play up the ground with an elite work rate and is dangerous closer to home as an aerialist that butters up at ground level.

Lochie Burrows has been closely linked with the Dragons product providing the toughness, running power and versatility Ross Lyon covets. He can play at either end before eventually moving on-ball, but the Saints would be risking losing out on him if they leave it to pick 16. Leo Steed remains a live option as a pure midfielder that can unlock the runners around him with clean hands in stoppages. The wildcard at this spot is Jack Pickett whose excellent forward craft saw him enter the season at the top key forward prospect before rupturing his ACL.

On night two the Saints can address forward-half woes with talent including powerful SA small Gabe Patterson or exciting goalkicker Marlon Neocleous. Depending on their first two selections, the talls around the mark will include WA's Harvey Spawton-Guy and Knights defender Tate Hodgson.

Sydney
Draft picks: 6, 38, 39, 47, 54, 76, 95, 113

List needs: Key defensive talent, midfield youth

The Swans have their first top 10 pick since taking Logan McDonald and Braeden Campbell in 2020, courtesy of Nick Blakey's exit.

It's a good spot to swoop on any slider out of the top bracket of the open pool. A quality key defensive prospect will be circled on the whiteboard with SA's Mitch Harris the standout this year. He's the all-round package that can lockdown and intercept with safe hands and good closing speed. If there was a name to slide it could be Gus Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder that will eventually become a full-time on-baller.

Expect Sydney to have a good look at a bid on Ethan Matthews out of the Giants Academy, which GWS will promptly match. They may be on the receiving end of an early bid themselves, with Mason McGroder attracting plenty of attention as early as the second round. The champion long jumper has chosen to pursue football and, while raw, he offers incredible upside as a defender that attacks the ball in the air.

As a key forward that can impact right away, Jack Slattery was the best-performed player at the national championships and is just one year older than the draft class. The SA prospect is slightly undersized at 192cm but is a beautiful set shot and creates separation on the lead. His range begins in the 30s. Koby LeCras has a chance to be on the board still after a partial tear of his ACL, but the hard-running forward can play a variety of roles at 192cm including up on a wing or deep forward.

West Coast
Draft picks: 3, 23, 58, 64, 73, 82, 100 (plus second round compensation pick)

List needs: Best available talent

West Coast have another top pick to capitalise on as their list build takes shape. They're right in the frame to snap up the most highly-touted WA prospect since Luke Jackson, with classy midfielder Heath Mellody deserving of a top five pick this year. Beginning his season out of defence, Mellody blossomed on-ball winning the Larke Medal and dominating in patches at WAFL level for Claremont. He has an insatiable work ethic and uses the ball well in space, attributes that pair well alongside Harley Reid and Willem Duursma in the engine room.

It's not a foregone conclusion that the Eagles opt for the local product. Expect them to heavily consider Arki Butler if the goalkicker is on the board still with a real need to add firepower to the forward 50 alongside Jake Waterman. Ethan Drever's power out of the contest will also be coveted and it would be another Vic Country prospect to join the pick one duo.

There's a familial connection with the nephew of 2018 premiership forward Mark LeCras. Koby possesses real talent at 192cm with his running, smarts and goal sense allowing him to play inside 50 or up on a wing. He's a second round option, as is hard nut Noah Williams whose courage in the clinches and capacity to play with defensive intent has value. Local product George Gale has the frame to play early through the midfield and wings in this range as well.

The Eagles will look to trade one of their second round selections for a 2026 first-rounder with an eye towards capital for a Chad Warner play. Add to it that James Artemis is a top prospect in the crop out of Western Australia.

It comes with the list crunch - West Coast has three spots to use at the national draft and will be keen to secure father-son Harper Banfield after missing on brother Charlie last year. Halfback Garrison Kenh and father-son Noah Braun will be rookie considerations.

Western Bulldogs
Draft picks: 42, 53, 55, 83, 89, 91, 109

List needs: Reliable role players, small forward depth

The Dogs did their work at the trade period by securing Zak Butters via free agency and a multi-club trade. It means they enter proceedings late on night two with an eye towards talented NGA forward Khaled El Souki. He's rated around the top 20 but may slide due to the depth of the crop which will make for an easier time matching a bid for the Dogs.

They addressed their key defensive dearth with Jordon Butts but should still have a look at Xavier Ladbrook as a long-term piece, and there are more defensive options in Darcy Szerszyn and Billy Wigmore that could be available later in the draft. Wigmore is a local Western Jets product alongside Lachie Hicks whose athletic traits through the midfield are tempting.
