stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: Watching successor Kimi Antonelli win title 'highlight of my year'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.

Antonelli, who replaced the seven-time world champion at Mercedes at the start of 2025 following his move to Ferrari, clinched the title at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest champion in F1 history at just 20 years old.

Hamilton, along with fellow multiple title-winner Max Verstappen, celebrated Antonelli's achievement on the podium and praised the Italian in a post on social media on Monday.

"Let me start with a huge congratulations to the new champion, Kimi Antonelli," Hamilton, 41, wrote on Instagram. "To have seen your journey so closely and to be there celebrating with you, was a highlight of my year. So well deserved and a record that will stand for a long time.

"It was great to see your team at Mercedes celebrating with you. Enjoy this moment, keep your family close, keep your passion and your energy."

Antonelli was just 18 when he stepped into Hamilton's seat at Mercedes, facing the daunting task of replacing the most successful driver in F1 history, who won six of his seven world titles with the Silver Arrows.

But the Italian has enjoyed a remarkable second season, beating teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Hamilton -- among others -- to the championship with four rounds still scheduled to take place.

Hamilton's congratulations came alongside an admission of frustration over Ferrari's weekend in Mexico, where he felt the team had missed an opportunity to win and also appeared to acknowledge tensions following Charles Leclerc's actions on the opening laps.

"Our own weekend was one full of challenges," Hamilton said. "We had a lot thrown at us but our mechanics and engineers did an incredible job.

"We've grown so much together this year, and that progress has taken a huge effort from everyone on the track and back at the factory. That's why losing what could've been a win hurts so much.

"We need to grasp every opportunity we have, so it's incredibly frustrating, and I can't pretend otherwise."

- Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari have 'big problems' after Charles Leclerc incident

- Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari, questions Leclerc's 'mentality'

He added: "Battling is necessary, but when that battle costs the team, we have to be honest about it and learn from it.

"We can push each other to the limit and still honour the responsibility to everyone who put us on that track."

Despite his frustrations, Hamilton insisted his commitment to Ferrari remained unchanged.

"I'll keep giving everything I have. My belief in this team hasn't changed and neither has my responsibility to help us get this right," he said.

"Stick with us. I'm only just getting started with this team, and we have so much more to come."

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up
stories.summary: Which teams are in the best position heading into Decision Day? All this and more in the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday and another weekend of action is in the books. With Decision Day coming up next week, it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings to see which teams are in a good or bad spot to qualify for the MLS Cup playoffs.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While seeking history on a rainy night in Tennessee, Nashville fell behind by two goals, had multiple goals called off, but battled back to force two own goals and clinch a 3-2 win against Red Bull New York with stoppage-time headed goal from Sam Surridge. The Supporters' Shield winners are level with Miami's points record, but could break it with just a point from their final game.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Miami reclaimed second place in the Eastern Conference with a second-half rally against the Revs to win 2-1, ignited by the guy still leading the Golden Boot race: Lionel Messi. After a headed assist to Germán Berterame to level the score, Messi scored his 26th goal of the year after finagling past multiple defenders then sending a low left-footed strike past Matt Turner.

3. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 4

The Revs' four-game win streak came to a halt against the Herons, as Messi proved the difference maker once more assisting and scoring in a come-from-behind win for Miami. With that, New England drops to third place in the Eastern Conference. Silver lining? Dániel Gazdag is now on a two-game scoring streak.

4. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

STL had the firepower in the attacking third to come away with all three points against San Diego. But thanks in part to Pablo Sisniega's six saves and Anders Dreyer's moment of quality, they went home with a 1-0 defeat instead. The playoffs were already locked up but home-field advantage isn't as they head into the final weekend.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

After going scoreless in six games, Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to make the difference in Colorado, providing the go-ahead goal 10 minutes after subbing on, then setting up Puso Dithejane for the 4-2 win.

6. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 7

The Whitecaps showed their quality in a comprehensive 5-1 dismantling of Seattle, highlighted by a Brian White brace that started in the 56th minute. After a 4-1 win over San Diego in midweek and 29th-place Montréal up next, the Western Conference's first-place side have got some momentum ahead of the postseason.

7. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

After drawing Nashville 0-0 in the midweek, Philly's 1-0 loss to Cincinnati is their second in three games. They'll be in the postseason, but they may have a tough matchup when it comes.

8. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 9

With the Golden Boot technically still in reach, Petar Musa (who scored 22 goals this season) missed his first penalty in six this season in the 97th minute. Stefan Cleveland's late-game save kept the Toros from three points in a 1-1 draw as they head into the final weekend looking to secure second place in the Western Conference.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

After losing 3-1 to Minnesota, LAFC are winless in three (two draws) ahead of a Decision Day battle with the Sounders. With their playoff place secure, they're competing for a better finish in the standings, but will fall short of their top-three finish in the Western Conference in the last four seasons.

10. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Kristijan Kahlina, whose save percentage (75.9%) is second only to first-place Nashville's Brian Schwake (77.7%), stopped eight against Orlando in a match that ended 4-0 in Charlotte's favor, despite both teams firing off the same number of shots (and nearly the same on target, though Charlotte had higher quality opportunities).

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 11

After losing 4-0 to mid-table side Charlotte, Orlando picked up their first defeat in six games but still clinched their playoff spot based on other results. They're in the final wild card spot ahead of a final test against the Revs.

12. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

The Quakes took 17 minutes to score twice against RSL, and that was enough to secure three points in a 2-1 win. That's their first win in six (four draws, one loss) as they look to secure their third-place spot in the Western Conference.

13. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

In a 5-1 loss to Vancouver, Jordan Morris' brief light of life in the second half was overshadowed by the Whitecaps' rapid response in a match characterized by goalkeeper Andy Thomas looking painfully skyward for help from the scoreline. After losing to Houston in midweek, the Sounders have three defeats and no wins from their last five games. They play LAFC on the final day while sitting one place short of the wild card spots.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 14

Morgan Whittaker scored from close range to mark his third goal in three games and take an early 1-0 lead against Chicago. But at the end of a goal-heavy matchup, Lewandowski scored and assisted off the bench to help see the Fire to a 4-2 win. The Rapids ended the weekend in the final playoff position and have a tough final test against Dallas to hang on.

15. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 17

Cincinnati only forced one save out of Andre Blake, but with the help of Roman Celentano's six stops, they booked their playoff spot with a 1-0 win against the Union. Ayoub Jabbari came off the bench in the second half and registered the sole tally of the night, capitalizing on Blake's save (a low-struck ball from Evander) to score off the rebound.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 16

The Dynamo could secure home advantage in the playoffs with a top-of-the-table finish, but are hanging on to fifth place ahead of the final day after losing 3-1 to Portland (their first loss in six). They have a decisive meeting with St. Louis on the final day, who are just ahead of them on goal difference but tied on points.

17. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 19

Sergi Roberto's first MLS goal was the icing on the cake of a 4-1 win against Austin that also featured Hirving Lozano's first goal back from injury and three assists from Marco Reus. Austin's not the toughest opponent in MLS this season, but the result matters as the Galaxy head into the final weekend still competing for a playoff spot.

18. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 20

The Crew may have lost the U.S. Open Cup final, but after beating D.C United 3-0, they're finishing the regular season on a five-game win streak. They confirmed their spot in the postseason and finished the weekend in one of the Eastern Conference's two wild card positions.

19. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 22

The Timbers secured a massive three points in a 3-1 win against the Dynamo highlighted by two assists and a goal from Vincent Janssen (nearly half his total goal contributions this year). With one game remaining, they're in a wild card spot and have one tentative hand on the playoffs.

20. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 23

In his first start since September, Joaquín Pereyra powered the Loons to three points with two goals against LAFC in a 3-1 win. They're still short of a final playoff spot (by two points) but following this result, they can still potentially break in with a win (and other results going in their favor), with San Jose waiting on the final day.

21. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

After falling behind 2-0 early to San Jose, Juan Manuel Sanabria's headed goal (his second of the year) in the 23rd minute provided life, but unfortunately nothing followed. They're currently outside the wild card spots ahead of a crucial final game against the Galaxy, but will also need some results to go their way.

22. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 12

RBNY had an early penalty stopped but came out with the upper hand against Nashville, taking a 2-0 lead in Tennessee that started with a beautiful link up between league wonderkids Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall. But after two own goals and a stoppage-time winner from Nashville, the Red Bulls were eliminated from the playoffs in consecutive seasons for the first time ever.

23. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 21

After conceding a 91st-minute goal to last-placed Montréal, the Pigeons' playoff chances are officially over. A 1-1 draw isn't enough to launch them into the wild card position with one more game to go.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 26

Dreyer -- a back-to-back MLS All-Star -- won't feature in this year's postseason, but that didn't stop him from handing the recently-crowded U.S. Open Cup champions a loss in a 1-0 victory over St. Louis. Dreyer's left-footed chip from distance was a taste of quality we'll be missing seven days from now.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 24

With no postseason hopes, victories must come from small achievements, like letting Reus assist three goals or having a goalkeeper make six saves while still conceding four.

26. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

Toronto succumbed to a 3-1 defeat to Atlanta and ended their postseason dream in the process. Back to the drawing board for Robin Fraser's side, who showed signs of potential earlier in the season.

27. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 28

With the playoffs out of the picture and the all-time goals conceded in a single season record newly secured, SKC still did their best to sabotage Dallas by absconding with a 1-1 draw against a side looking to lock up their top-two finish in the Western Conference.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 29

Miguel Almirón won't appear in this year's playoffs, so he put on an end-of-season show in a 3-1 win against Toronto while eliminating the fellow Eastern Conference team from the playoffs. Five Stripes fans will take what they can get this year.

29. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

After losing to Toronto in the midweek, D.C. played Columbus with the playoffs already out of the picture and proceeded to lose 3-0. With 11 years since their last postseason victory, there's nowhere to go but up for this MLS original.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

It's too late to save their season, but not too late to sink somebody else's. A 91st-minute response to NYCFC's 1-0 lead secured their 26th point of the year and put to rest New York's postseason dream.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Cowboys keen on Raiders' Savage
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news on Bradman Best's future and which clubs might be lining up a play for Sam Walker.
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Cowboys among clubs eyeing Savage

North Queensland are among the clubs showing interest in Canberra winger Xavier Savage, as rivals assess their recruitment options for 2028.

ESPN understands the Cowboys and a Sydney-based club are keeping tabs on the speedster, who is contracted to the Raiders until the end of 2027 and became eligible to negotiate with rivals on November 1.

Savage scored 13 tries in 19 NRL appearances for Canberra this season.

Bryenton begins Tigers chapter

David Bryenton will begin full-time training with the Wests Tigers on Wednesday, with ESPN understanding the recruit features in Benji Marshall's long-term plans.

Having first reported his signing last month, ESPN can reveal Bryenton's mutually agreed release from the Bulldogs has now been finalised, clearing the way for him to join Marshall's squad for pre-season.

Dolphins win race for Su'a

The Dolphins have won the race to retain Sebastian Su'a, with ESPN understanding the young forward has agreed to terms on a two-year extension that will keep him in Redcliffe until the end of 2029.

Several NRL clubs had identified Su'a as a potential recruitment target, but the Dolphins have moved to secure his future with the club.

Fa'alogo agrees to long-term Storm extension

Sua Fa'alogo has agreed to extend his stay at the Melbourne Storm through to the end of 2032, ESPN understands.

The agreement will keep the fullback in Melbourne for the next six seasons, securing a key figure in the Storm's long-term plans.

Fa'alogo's retention delivers a major boost for Melbourne ahead of the November 1 contracting window, with the club moving to lock down one of its most exciting talents.

Dolphins close in on Lemuelu extension, confident of keeping Farnworth

The Dolphins are closing in on a multi-year extension for Connelly Lemuelu as they also express confidence in retaining Herbie Farnworth.

ESPN understands Lemuelu is nearing an agreement to extend his stay despite interest from Canberra, Parramatta and Cronulla.

Securing the back-rower would deliver a retention boost for the Dolphins, with the length of the proposed deal yet to be confirmed.

The club is also understood to be confident it can retain Farnworth despite links to the Sydney Roosters.

While that confidence is yet to translate into a confirmed extension, keeping the English international alongside Lemuelu would help preserve key combinations on the Dolphins' left edge.

Eels edge ahead in Best race
Parramatta have emerged as the frontrunners to land Bradman Best, with multiple sources indicating the Newcastle centre is increasingly likely to join the Eels beyond 2027.

Best has been identified as a priority target for Parramatta, who are looking to bolster Jason Ryles' backline with an established representative star.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the Eels are understood to be in the box seat despite Newcastle's efforts to retain him with a lucrative extension.

Bulldogs unlikely to enter Walker race
Canterbury are unlikely to enter the race for Sam Walker, with the Bulldogs backing their existing halfback options ahead of the upcoming season.

Despite suggestions the club could emerge as a potential destination for Walker, it is understood Canterbury are taking a wait-and-see approach rather than preparing to launch a pursuit.

The Bulldogs' immediate focus remains on the internal battle for the No.7 jersey, with Mitch and Alex Conti set to compete for the role over the offseason.

Canterbury have not completely shut the door on a move should circumstances change, but their current position suggests they are unlikely to become an active contender for Walker's signature.

For now, the Bulldogs are content to watch how the situation unfolds.
